rules.title: Landlord prohibition on upfront charges other than first, last, security deposit and lock (G.L. c. 186, § 15B), as described by a secondary source
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a lessor may require payment of only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock charge. The secondary source reads this as barring landlord-charged application, screening, pet, cleaning and amenity fees. Licensed brokers are described as able to charge application fees under 254 CMR 7.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security and lock charges allowed before tenancy begins; landlord application fees barred (per secondary source); no dollar cap stated

coverage.summary: Applies to lessors of residential tenancies; the passages state no unit-count or building-age limits.

rules.exemptions: Licensed brokers may charge application fees per the secondary source (254 CMR 7); the statute text is not in the passages.
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks (MGL Ch 186 Section 15B).
rules.review_note: Secondary blog source; the statute text itself is not in the passages. The broker-fee point rests on the same blog. Verify against the statute.
rules.source_notes: Blog also cites Perry v. Equity Residential Management (federal district court, 2014) as finding up-front application fees unlawful.

rules.title: Broker licensing and tenant-paid finder fees (G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD1/2, as amended eff. Aug. 1, 2025)
rules.requirement: No person may find dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless a licensed broker or salesperson. The amended text effective Aug. 1, 2025 adds that a licensed broker or salesperson may solely contract with a prospective tenant to find rental residential real property. The passage is cut off, so the rest of the fee-allocation language is unavailable.

coverage.summary: Applies to persons in the business of finding rental dwellings for tenants for a fee.

rules.effective_date_note: The licensing sentence was already in the text effective until Aug. 1, 2025. The amendment by 2025, c. 9, § 43 takes effect Aug. 1, 2025 (per 2025, 9, Sec. 136).
